questions.question: When you ride, the best gear to wear is:

options.text: Gear that protects you.
The cheapest gear available.
Gear that looks good.
Any gear that fits.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gear that protects you.
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. A DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing are best.

questions.question: A danger of riding next to parked cars is:

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
Others may drive slowly while looking for a spot.
The road may be uneven.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
questions.explanation: Riding next to parked cars is dangerous. A driver might pull out without looking. Car doors may open into your lane. Pedestrians may step out between cars.

questions.question: Before mounting a motorcycle, you should check all of the following, except:

options.text: The air pressure in the tires.
Fluid levels.
The turn signals.
Paint damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Paint damage.
questions.explanation: Before getting on a motorcycle, check the tire tread and air pressure, oil and fluid levels, lights, and signals.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection usually takes:

options.text: A few minutes and should be done once a month.
A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
Over an hour and must be done by a mechanic.
Over an hour and only needed when carrying a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-ride inspection before every ride. It takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle:

options.text: Skip checking the tire pressure.
Expect it to handle like your own bike.
The owner will check the brakes for you.
Give yourself extra space and time to react.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give yourself extra space and time to react.
questions.explanation: Do all safety checks on a borrowed motorcycle just like on your own. Ride carefully with an unfamiliar bike and allow extra stopping distance.

questions.question: If you ride on the right side of your lane while following a car:

options.text: You are likely in the best position to be seen.
The driver may not see you unless they check their side mirror.
The driver will know you are there.
You discourage other riders from sharing your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may not see you unless they check their side mirror.
questions.explanation: When following a car, ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors.

questions.question: When preparing to pass, ride in the left portion of your lane because:

options.text: It helps you see better ahead.
It makes it harder to see ahead.
It blocks your view of the vehicle.
It lets the other driver speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you see better ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This improves your view and makes you more visible to drivers in the passing lane.

questions.question: Keep extra space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead when:

options.text: Stopping will be harder than usual.
You want to look at the scenery.
You want other drivers to cut in front.
You want to hide from the driver ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping will be harder than usual.
questions.explanation: Use extra space when your bike needs more time to stop. Increase your distance on slippery roads, when you cannot see ahead, or in heavy traffic.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Shifting into a lower gear has an effect like:

options.text: Using the brakes.
Accelerating.
Swerving.
Turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using the brakes.
questions.explanation: Shifting into a lower gear slows your motorcycle like using the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: Riding at night is usually:

options.text: Easier than riding during the day because you can see other vehicle lights more easily.
Harder than riding during the day because it is harder to see.
Not allowed on highways.
Less distracting than riding during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than riding during the day because it is harder to see.
questions.explanation: Riding at night is harder because you cannot see as well as during the day. Without natural light and shadows, it is harder to judge distances.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should choose footwear with soles that:

options.text: Are hard, durable, and slip-resistant.
Allow their feet to breathe.
Have tall heels.
Are soft and flimsy.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are hard, durable, and slip-resistant.
questions.explanation: Choose riding boots or shoes that are high and sturdy to support your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: If a friend has had too much to drink and wants to ride their motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Let them ride.
Encourage them to use quiet roads.
Not get involved.
Take their keys.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take their keys.
questions.explanation: Never let someone ride if they have had too much to drink. Stop them from riding by taking their keys if necessary. Help them find another way to get home.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should ride:

options.text: In any part of the lane.
In the part of the lane closest to the shoulder.
In the part of the lane where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
As close to the car as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the part of the lane where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position your motorcycle so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Usually, this means riding in the center of the lane. Drivers check rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position makes it more likely they will see you.

questions.question: When riding, goggles:

options.text: Protect your eyes, but not the rest of your face.
Protect your face, but not your eyes.
Do not protect your eyes as well as eyeglasses.
Do not provide any protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your eyes, but not the rest of your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only. A face shield is needed to protect your entire face. Eyeglasses are not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: To get the best protection, be sure that your helmet:

options.text: Meets Department of Transportation guidelines.
Looks sturdy.
Is inexpensive.
Is your favorite color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Meets Department of Transportation guidelines.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no obvious defects.

questions.question: What type of clothing material offers the best protection to motorcyclists?

options.text: Leather
Wool
Polyester
Silk

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather clothing provides the best protection for motorcyclists. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs completely when riding.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
Should be avoided because they distract you.
Should be avoided because other drivers can see you easily.
Are only recommended in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: It is important to know what is behind you. Check your mirrors often as part of your normal scanning routine.

questions.question: When approaching an uneven surface, such as a bump or pothole, you should rise slightly off your seat:

options.text: So you can jump off the motorcycle if needed.
So your legs can absorb the shock.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can get a better view of the uneven surface.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your joints absorb some of the impact force. This helps prevent the bump from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Restricts side vision.
Can greatly reduce head injury severity.
Is usually uncomfortable.
Makes it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can greatly reduce head injury severity.
questions.explanation: Wearing a DOT-approved helmet greatly reduces the risk of serious head or neck injury in a crash. It does not restrict your side vision.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?

options.text: At night.
Not during the day.
Never.
Not at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: At night.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective clothing at night to make yourself more visible to other drivers. Bright colors and reflective materials help other road users see you.

questions.question: If you wait one hour for each drink before riding, what happens?

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your skills will not be affected.
Alcohol effects may still remain.
You will be fine if you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still remain.
questions.explanation: Your body can eliminate about one drink per hour. But alcohol can still build up in your system. This can affect your ability to ride safely, even if you wait between drinks.

questions.question: Why wear a leather jacket when riding?

options.text: It makes you look cool.
It is too warm to wear.
It protects you in a crash.
You should not wear one.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved leather jacket when riding for crash protection. Leather jackets are designed to protect you and keep you cool even in hot weather.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good choice for riding clothes?

options.text: A jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs.
Boots or shoes that cover your ankles.
Leather gloves.
A baseball cap.

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap.
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots or shoes that support your ankles, and durable gloves. A baseball cap does not provide proper head protection.

questions.question: When adjusting your rearview mirror, what should you see?

options.text: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
Only the lane behind you.
Only the lane next to you.
Most of your helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and the lane next to you. The road behind and to the side is most important to watch.
